<thought>From the spectrum, the dominant isotopic pattern is a strong M peak at 114, with an M+1 peak at ~6.7% intensity and rapidly decreasing higher isotopes. This matches the natural 13C distribution (≈1.1 % per carbon), indicating the presence of carbon. No characteristic 3:1 (Cl) or 1:1 (Br) patterns are seen, and the M+2 intensity is far below the ~4 % expected for sulfur. Thus, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
